newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on ample feedgrain supplies.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on ample feedgrain supplies.

text.p: Abundant supplies of feedgrains amid little fresh news allowed scattered selling to press CBOT corn futures to a lower close, traders said.
"There were no bullish fundamentals," a trader said. Corn early tried to hold up with wheat and beans but when soybean futures broke late, corn also sagged.
Traders again cited the recent bearish USDA crop production report and heavy yields this year of sorghum as keeping a cap on corn futures values.
"The biggest feature are the spreads widening out. Unwinding of spreads and liquidation in December," he said.

December was faltering in early dealings against other contracts. But in late trade Dec began to recover on spreads with the December/March closing at 2-1/2 cents per bushel premium March, a 3/4 cent narrowing of that spread.
"There's plenty of feedgrain around and if the spreads are no good corn is going a lot lower," the trader said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 52,000 contracts, below the 72,643 traded Monday, according to the CBOT.
Corn closed 1/2 to two cents per bushel lower, with December down 3/4 at $2.65-1/4 a bushel.
